summary: Count records, including rows with missing fields.
syntax: SELECT COUNT(*) AS count_name FROM table_name;
documentation: COUNT(*) counts rows in the selected input. COUNT(expression) instead counts rows where that expression is not NULL.
inputs: A table or filtered set of rows.
caution: COUNT(column) can undercount records when that column is NULL.
scenarios: Count incoming leads even when a contact field is missing.
Count bookings in a time range.
Measure how many orders need review.
title: Count pending orders
problem: Return one column called pending_count containing the number of orders with status = 'pending'.
goal: Use COUNT(*) or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Use COUNT(*) and a WHERE filter.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Mixed orders
tests.setup:
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER, customer TEXT, amount_cents INTEGER, status TEXT);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 'Ava', 100, 'pending'), (2, 'Micki', 200, 'paid'), (3, NULL, 300, 'pending');

tests.name: Nothing pending
